questions.question: A data team has a container that reads a day's files, writes a report and exits, typically after 20 minutes. It runs once a day, serves no HTTP traffic, and the team wants no infrastructure to manage. Which platform should it use?

options.A: Cloud Run services
options.B: Compute Engine with a managed instance group
options.C: GKE Standard with a Deployment
options.D: Cloud Run jobs

explanation.summary: Cloud Run jobs run containers to completion with no servers or cluster, and bill only while tasks run.

option_breakdown.A: A service must listen for requests and is scaled by them; a job that exits fits it badly.
option_breakdown.B: A MIG keeps VMs running and is managed infrastructure the team wants to avoid.
option_breakdown.C: A Deployment restarts containers that exit, which is the opposite of run-to-completion.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. Cloud Run jobs run containers to completion with no servers or cluster, and bill only while tasks run.

questions.title: A licensed Windows Server application
questions.summary: Applications that need a specific OS, such as Windows Server with licensed software, run on Compute Engine.
questions.question: An accounting package runs only on Windows Server with a locally installed licence service and a desktop installer; it cannot be containerised. The company is moving it to Google Cloud this quarter. Which platform should it use?

options.A: Compute Engine VMs running Windows Server.
options.B: Cloud Run, with the installer baked into a container image.
options.C: GKE Autopilot, with Windows node pools.
options.D: Cloud Run functions, one per accounting task.

explanation.summary: Compute Engine gives full control of the operating system, including Windows Server images and installed licence services — the lift-and-shift answer when the software cannot be containerised.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. Compute Engine gives full control of the operating system, including Windows Server images and installed licence services — the lift-and-shift answer when the software cannot be containerised.
option_breakdown.B: Cloud Run runs Linux containers; a Windows desktop installer cannot become one.
option_breakdown.C: Autopilot does not offer Windows nodes, and the application cannot be containerised anyway.
option_breakdown.D: Functions run small handlers in managed Linux runtimes.

questions.title: A clean-up task every night at 02:00
questions.summary: A Kubernetes CronJob runs a Job on a schedule inside the cluster.
questions.question: A GKE-hosted application needs a container to delete expired sessions from its database every night at 02:00, using the same image and credentials as the application's other workloads. Which Kubernetes object should you create?

options.A: A DaemonSet that sleeps until 02:00 on every node.
options.B: A Deployment with one replica running a loop that checks the clock.
options.C: A StatefulSet with one replica and a persistent volume.
options.D: A CronJob with the schedule "0 2 * * *".

explanation.summary: A CronJob creates a Job on a cron schedule; the Job runs the container to completion and records success or failure.

option_breakdown.A: A DaemonSet runs a copy on every node, so the clean-up would run many times.
option_breakdown.B: A looping Deployment holds resources all day and reimplements scheduling.
option_breakdown.C: StatefulSets give stable identity and storage to long-running replicas, not scheduled tasks.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. A CronJob creates a Job on a cron schedule; the Job runs the container to completion and records success or failure.

questions.title: How many nodes a regional cluster really creates
questions.summary: In a regional cluster, --num-nodes is per zone, so three zones multiply it by three.
questions.question: An engineer creates a GKE Standard regional cluster in europe-central2 with --num-nodes=2, expecting two nodes in total for a small test. The region has three zones. How many nodes are created?

options.A: Two — spread across two of the zones.
options.B: Six — two in each of the region's three zones.
options.C: Two — both in the region's first zone.
options.D: Three — one per zone, the minimum for a regional cluster.

explanation.summary: For a regional cluster, --num-nodes sets the node count per zone, and nodes are placed in three zones by default, so 2 becomes 6.

option_breakdown.A: The flag is per zone, not a cluster total.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. For a regional cluster, --num-nodes sets the node count per zone, and nodes are placed in three zones by default, so 2 becomes 6.
option_breakdown.C: A regional cluster spreads nodes across its zones rather than using one.
option_breakdown.D: The requested per-zone count is honoured; there is no forced minimum of one per zone here.

explanation.gcloud_command: gcloud container clusters create test --location=europe-central2 --num-nodes=1   # = 3 nodes

questions.title: What gcloud compute ssh does the first time
questions.summary: Without OS Login, gcloud compute ssh generates a key pair and adds the public key to metadata.
questions.question: On a project without OS Login, a developer runs gcloud compute ssh web-1 for the first time from a new laptop and is connected after a short wait. No administrator added a key. What did gcloud do?

options.A: Downloaded the instance's host private key to the laptop.
options.B: Generated a key pair and published the public key to metadata.
options.C: Created a service-account key for the developer and used it to log in.
options.D: Opened port 22 to the internet with a temporary firewall rule.

explanation.summary: gcloud compute ssh creates ~/.ssh/google_compute_engine if needed and publishes its public key to metadata, where the guest agent creates the user and authorises the key.

option_breakdown.A: Host private keys never leave the VM.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. gcloud compute ssh creates ~/.ssh/google_compute_engine if needed and publishes its public key to metadata, where the guest agent creates the user and authorises the key.
option_breakdown.C: Service-account keys are not SSH credentials.
option_breakdown.D: gcloud does not create firewall rules; the path must already be allowed.

questions.title: More memory per vCPU than any standard shape
questions.summary: Extended memory lets a custom machine type exceed the normal memory-per-vCPU limit.
questions.question: A licensed in-memory cache is charged per vCPU, so the team wants only 8 vCPUs but needs 160 GB of memory — more than the maximum memory per vCPU of a normal custom N2 shape. What should they create?

options.A: An n2-highmem-32 predefined machine type.
options.B: An 8-vCPU VM with a 160 GB Local SSD used as swap.
options.C: Two 8-vCPU VMs with 80 GB each.
options.D: A custom N2 shape with 8 vCPUs and extended memory.

explanation.summary: Extended memory allows a custom machine type to have more memory than the standard per-vCPU ceiling, which keeps the vCPU count — and the licence cost — low.

option_breakdown.A: 32 vCPUs would quadruple the per-vCPU licence cost.
option_breakdown.B: Swap on disk is far slower than memory and defeats an in-memory cache.
option_breakdown.C: Splitting the cache doubles the licensed vCPUs and changes the application's design.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. Extended memory allows a custom machine type to have more memory than the standard per-vCPU ceiling, which keeps the vCPU count — and the licence cost — low.

questions.title: Relational data with zero loss across regions
questions.summary: Spanner multi-region configurations replicate synchronously with automatic failover and zero RPO.
questions.question: An order-management database must remain writable if an entire region is lost, lose no committed transaction, and fail over without anyone promoting a replica. It is relational and uses SQL transactions. What should you deploy?

options.A: A Spanner instance with a multi-region configuration.
options.B: Cloud SQL with high availability and a cross-region read replica.
options.C: Cloud SQL with high availability only.
options.D: Firestore in a multi-region location.

explanation.summary: Spanner's multi-region configurations replicate synchronously across regions with automatic failover, so committed data survives a region with no manual step.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. Spanner's multi-region configurations replicate synchronously across regions with automatic failover, so committed data survives a region with no manual step.
option_breakdown.B: A cross-region replica is asynchronous (some data loss) and must be promoted by someone.
option_breakdown.C: Cloud SQL HA protects against a zone failure, not a region.
option_breakdown.D: Firestore is a document database; it does not provide the relational SQL transactions required.

questions.title: Objects that must stay in two named regions
questions.summary: A configurable dual-region bucket keeps data in two regions you choose and survives the loss of either.
questions.question: Regulations require that a company's documents be stored only in Frankfurt and Warsaw (europe-west3 and europe-central2), and remain readable if either region is lost, with no failover step. What should you create?

options.A: A multi-region bucket in EU.
options.B: A regional bucket in each region, with the application writing to both.
options.C: A regional bucket in europe-west3 with object versioning.
options.D: A dual-region bucket in europe-west3 and europe-central2.

explanation.summary: A dual-region bucket (configurable) stores data redundantly in exactly the two regions named, and serves reads from either if one is lost.

option_breakdown.A: The EU multi-region may place data in regions other than the two allowed.
option_breakdown.B: Dual writes from the application push consistency and failure handling onto your code.
option_breakdown.C: Versioning protects against overwrites and deletes, not against a region outage.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. A dual-region bucket (configurable) stores data redundantly in exactly the two regions named, and serves reads from either if one is lost.

questions.title: 600 TB over a 200 Mbps link
questions.summary: When volume over available bandwidth takes too long, ship the data with Transfer Appliance.
questions.question: A research institute must move 600 TB of archived imaging data to Cloud Storage within two months. Its internet link is 200 Mbps and is shared with daily operations. What should it use?

options.A: Storage Transfer Service with an on-premises agent pool.
options.B: gcloud storage rsync from a server in the data centre.
options.C: BigQuery Data Transfer Service.
options.D: Transfer Appliance.

explanation.summary: At 200 Mbps — about 2 TB a day at full, uncontended speed — 600 TB takes the best part of a year; shipping the data on an appliance meets the deadline.

option_breakdown.A: Agent-based transfers still move every byte over the same 200 Mbps link.
option_breakdown.B: rsync has the same bandwidth ceiling, with less management.
option_breakdown.C: BigQuery Data Transfer Service loads data into BigQuery from SaaS and other sources; it is not bulk file migration.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. At 200 Mbps — about 2 TB a day at full, uncontended speed — 600 TB takes the best part of a year; shipping the data on an appliance meets the deadline.

explanation.gcloud_command: # Console > Transfer Appliance > Order an appliance

questions.title: Daily loads into BigQuery from Amazon S3
questions.summary: BigQuery Data Transfer Service schedules recurring loads from S3, SaaS apps and Cloud Storage into BigQuery.
questions.question: Partner files land in an Amazon S3 bucket every night as Parquet. Analysts want them appended to a BigQuery table each morning with no code to maintain and no staging pipeline. What should you set up?

options.A: A Compute Engine VM that downloads from S3 and runs bq load in a cron job.
options.B: A BigQuery Data Transfer Service transfer from Amazon S3 on a daily schedule.
options.C: Storage Transfer Service into Cloud Storage, then analysts run bq load each morning.
options.D: A Pub/Sub topic that the partner publishes the files to.

explanation.summary: BigQuery Data Transfer Service supports Amazon S3 as a source and loads the files into a BigQuery table on a schedule, managed and without code.

option_breakdown.A: A cron VM is code and infrastructure to maintain.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. BigQuery Data Transfer Service supports Amazon S3 as a source and loads the files into a BigQuery table on a schedule, managed and without code.
option_breakdown.C: This adds a staging step and a manual load every morning.
option_breakdown.D: Pub/Sub carries messages, not nightly Parquet files, and the partner writes to S3.

questions.title: A global load balancer in a Standard Tier project
questions.summary: Global external load balancers and global anycast IPs require Premium Tier.
questions.question: To save on egress, Ironbark Games set its project's default network tier to Standard. The team now needs a global external Application Load Balancer with one anycast IP address, serving players in Europe, Asia and North America. What must they do?

options.A: Keep Standard Tier; global load balancers work with either tier.
options.B: Use Premium Tier for the load balancer's IP address and forwarding rule.
options.C: Create one regional load balancer per continent on Standard Tier with the same IP.
options.D: Switch to Standard Tier's global mode on the forwarding rule.

explanation.summary: Global load balancing and global anycast IPs exist only on Premium Tier, which carries traffic on Google's backbone to the nearest edge; the tier can be set per resource even when the project default is Standard.

option_breakdown.A: Standard Tier is regional only and cannot front a global load balancer.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. Global load balancing and global anycast IPs exist only on Premium Tier, which carries traffic on Google's backbone to the nearest edge; the tier can be set per resource even when the project default is Standard.
option_breakdown.C: Regional load balancers each have their own regional IP; one IP cannot be shared across them.
option_breakdown.D: Standard Tier has no global mode.

questions.title: Standard Tier for every new resource in a project
questions.summary: The project default network tier sets the tier new resources receive unless overridden.
questions.question: A cost-sensitive project serves users in a single region and tolerates slightly higher latency. The team wants every VM and load balancer created from now on to use Standard Tier unless someone asks otherwise. What should they configure?

options.A: Reserve every external IP address in advance on Standard Tier.
options.B: Change each existing resource's tier and document the rule.
options.C: Set the project's default network tier to STANDARD.
options.D: Create a custom route that sends egress through the public internet.

explanation.summary: The project-level default network tier applies to resources created afterwards; individual resources can still override it.

option_breakdown.A: Pre-reserved addresses cover only the ones you reserve; anything created later still takes the project default.
option_breakdown.B: Changing existing resources does nothing for new ones.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. The project-level default network tier applies to resources created afterwards; individual resources can still override it.
option_breakdown.D: Routes decide next hops within the VPC; the tier decides how Google carries external traffic.

questions.title: One cheap regional endpoint in a Premium project
questions.summary: The network tier can be chosen per external IP address or forwarding rule, overriding the project default.
questions.question: A project defaults to Premium Tier for its global web application. A new VM that serves large, latency-tolerant file downloads to users in its own region should egress at the lower Standard Tier price. The rest of the project must stay on Premium. What should you do?

options.A: Change the project default network tier to Standard.
options.B: Move the VM to a new project whose default is Standard.
options.C: Give the VM's external IP address the Standard Tier.
options.D: Put the VM behind the global external Application Load Balancer.

explanation.summary: Network tier is a property of each external IP address or forwarding rule, so one resource can use Standard while the project default stays Premium.

option_breakdown.A: Changing the default would move new resources for the whole project to Standard.
option_breakdown.B: A new project works but is needless when the tier can be set per resource.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. Network tier is a property of each external IP address or forwarding rule, so one resource can use Standard while the project default stays Premium.
option_breakdown.D: The global load balancer is a Premium Tier product, the opposite of the goal.

questions.title: Secure tags that follow autoscaled GKE nodes
questions.subtopic: Secure Tags and Service Accounts in Rules
questions.summary: Set secure tags on a GKE node pool so every node it creates is selected by firewall policy rules.
questions.question: A global network firewall policy selects batch workers by the secure tag tier=batch. The workers are the nodes of a GKE Standard node pool that autoscales between 2 and 40 nodes, and every node must be covered by the policy from the moment it starts. What should you do?

options.A: Attach the tier=batch tag to each current node VM in Compute Engine.
options.B: Add the network tag batch to the node pool with --tags.
options.C: Label the batch Pods with tier=batch in their Deployment.
options.D: Create the node pool with the tier=batch secure tag on its nodes.

explanation.summary: GKE can attach secure tags to a node pool's nodes, so every node — including ones added by autoscaling or upgrades — carries the tag the firewall policy selects.

option_breakdown.A: Tags attached by hand are lost when nodes are recreated by autoscaling, repair or upgrade.
option_breakdown.B: Network tags work only in VPC firewall rules; firewall policies select by secure tags.
option_breakdown.C: Kubernetes labels are not network metadata; Cloud NGFW does not see them.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. GKE can attach secure tags to a node pool's nodes, so every node — including ones added by autoscaling or upgrades — carries the tag the firewall policy selects.

questions.title: Who may attach a secure tag to a VM
questions.subtopic: Secure Tags and Service Accounts in Rules
questions.summary: Binding a tag value to a resource needs roles/resourcemanager.tagUser on the value (and rights on the resource).
questions.question: Firewall policy rules select database VMs by the secure tag tier=db. Developers administer the VMs, but only the network team may decide which VMs fall under the db rules. How is this enforced?

options.A: Grant Tag User on the tier=db value only to the network team.
options.B: Grant developers roles/compute.securityAdmin instead of instance admin.
options.C: Use network tags, which only the network team can edit.
options.D: Label the database VMs, and restrict who may change labels.

explanation.summary: Attaching a secure tag value is itself an IAM-controlled action on the tag value; without Tag User on tier=db, a developer cannot put a VM under the db rules, however they edit the VM.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. Attaching a secure tag value is itself an IAM-controlled action on the tag value; without Tag User on tier=db, a developer cannot put a VM under the db rules, however they edit the VM.
option_breakdown.B: Security Admin manages firewall rules, which is broader and still does not control tag binding.
option_breakdown.C: Anyone who can edit an instance can change its network tags — the very weakness secure tags remove.
option_breakdown.D: Labels are not used by firewall rules at all.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud resource-manager tags values add-iam-policy-binding ORG_ID/tier/db \
  --member=group:net-team@example.com --role=roles/resourcemanager.tagUser

questions.title: Allowing only the app tier to reach the database tier
questions.subtopic: Secure Tags and Service Accounts in Rules
questions.summary: Firewall policy rules can match sources by secure tag as well as targets, expressing tier-to-tier intent.
questions.question: App VMs carry the secure tag tier=app and database VMs carry tier=db. Only app VMs may open TCP 5432 to database VMs, regardless of their IP addresses, which change with autoscaling. Which global network firewall policy rule expresses this?

options.A: An ingress allow rule for tcp:5432 from the app subnet's range to all instances.
options.B: An egress deny rule for tcp:5432 on every VM except the app tier.
options.C: An ingress allow rule for tcp:5432 from source network tag app to target network tag db.
options.D: An ingress allow for tcp:5432 from secure tag tier=app to tier=db.

explanation.summary: Firewall policy rules can select both the source and the target by secure tag, so the rule follows the tiers rather than addresses.

option_breakdown.A: A subnet range admits anything in that subnet, and targets every instance.
option_breakdown.B: Egress rules on other VMs do not express an allow for the app tier.
option_breakdown.C: Network tags are not used by firewall policy rules.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. Firewall policy rules can select both the source and the target by secure tag, so the rule follows the tiers rather than addresses.

questions.title: Allow and deny at the same priority
questions.summary: Among VPC firewall rules with the same priority that match, deny takes precedence over allow.
questions.question: A VPC has two ingress rules at priority 1000: one allows TCP 22 from 0.0.0.0/0 and one denies TCP 22 from 0.0.0.0/0, both applying to all instances. What happens to an SSH connection from the internet?

options.A: It is denied, because at equal priority a deny rule takes precedence.
options.B: It is allowed, because allow rules are evaluated first.
options.C: It is allowed or denied at random, depending on which rule was created first.
options.D: It is denied, because every ingress rule is overridden by the implied deny.

explanation.summary: Rules are evaluated by priority, and when rules with the same priority conflict, deny wins over allow.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. Rules are evaluated by priority, and when rules with the same priority conflict, deny wins over allow.
option_breakdown.B: Allow rules have no precedence at equal priority.
option_breakdown.C: Evaluation is deterministic; creation order does not matter.
option_breakdown.D: The implied deny ingress has the lowest priority, 65535, and applies only when no other rule matches.

questions.title: A new custom VPC with no rules at all
questions.summary: Every VPC has implied rules: allow all egress and deny all ingress, at the lowest priority.
questions.question: You create a custom-mode VPC with one subnet and no firewall rules, then two VMs in it, each with an external IP address. What does the firewall allow between the VMs and the internet?

options.A: Outbound connections only; no inbound, not even between the two VMs.
options.B: All traffic between the two VMs is allowed; only internet ingress is blocked.
options.C: No traffic is possible at all until an egress rule is created.
options.D: SSH and ICMP from anywhere are allowed, as in the default network.

explanation.summary: Without explicit rules, the implied rules apply: allow all egress, deny all ingress. Internal traffic is ingress to the receiving VM, so it is denied too.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. Without explicit rules, the implied rules apply: allow all egress, deny all ingress. Internal traffic is ingress to the receiving VM, so it is denied too.
option_breakdown.B: Internal traffic is not special; it needs an ingress allow rule like any other.
option_breakdown.C: Egress is allowed by the implied rule, so no egress rule is needed.
option_breakdown.D: SSH, ICMP and internal allows are pre-populated rules of the default network, not implied rules of new VPCs.

questions.title: Blocking traffic from specific countries
questions.summary: Cloud NGFW Standard adds geolocation objects to firewall policy rules.
questions.question: A regulator requires that the VMs of a payment service accept no connections from two named countries. The team wants the list maintained by Google rather than by tracking IP ranges itself. What should it use?

options.A: A VPC firewall rule that denies a list of IP ranges downloaded from a public registry.
options.B: An organisation policy restricting resource locations to other countries.
options.C: A firewall policy rule with a geolocation source for the two countries.
options.D: Private Google Access on the subnet.

explanation.summary: Cloud NGFW Standard lets firewall policy rules match sources by geolocation, so Google maintains the mapping from countries to addresses.

option_breakdown.A: A hand-maintained IP list goes stale and is exactly the tracking the team wants to avoid.
option_breakdown.B: Resource-location policy controls where resources are created, not where traffic comes from.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. Cloud NGFW Standard lets firewall policy rules match sources by geolocation, so Google maintains the mapping from countries to addresses.
option_breakdown.D: Private Google Access lets private VMs reach Google APIs; it filters nothing.

questions.title: Converting an auto-mode VPC
questions.summary: An auto-mode VPC can be converted to custom mode, but never back.
questions.question: A team started on an auto-mode VPC and now needs to control subnet ranges and regions itself, keeping the existing subnets and VMs. What should it do?

options.A: Delete the network and recreate it as custom mode with the same name.
options.B: Edit the auto-created subnets to custom mode one by one.
options.C: Convert the network to custom mode, keeping its subnets.
options.D: It cannot be done; auto-mode networks are permanent.

explanation.summary: Switching an auto-mode network to custom mode is supported and keeps its subnets; it is one-way — a custom network cannot become auto mode.

option_breakdown.A: Deleting the network would destroy the VMs' networking for no reason.
option_breakdown.B: Mode belongs to the network, not to individual subnets.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. Switching an auto-mode network to custom mode is supported and keeps its subnets; it is one-way — a custom network cannot become auto mode.
option_breakdown.D: Conversion to custom mode is supported.

questions.title: A service project team may use only its own subnet
questions.summary: Grant compute.networkUser on individual subnets of the host project for least privilege.
questions.question: Harbourline Shipping uses Shared VPC: the host project has one subnet for each of five teams. Developers in the customs team must create VMs in the customs subnet from their own service project, and must not be able to use any other team's subnet. What should you grant?

options.A: roles/compute.networkUser on the host project to team A's group.
options.B: roles/compute.networkAdmin on the host project to team A's group.
options.C: roles/compute.xpnAdmin on the organisation to team A's group.
options.D: roles/compute.networkUser on team A's subnet to team A's group.

explanation.summary: Network User granted on a single subnet lets the group create resources in that subnet and no other.

option_breakdown.A: Project-level Network User covers every subnet in the host project.
option_breakdown.B: Network Admin lets the team change the network itself.
option_breakdown.C: Shared VPC Admin enables host projects and attaches service projects — far beyond the need.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. Network User granted on a single subnet lets the group create resources in that subnet and no other.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud compute networks subnets add-iam-policy-binding team-a --region=REGION \
  --project=HOST_PROJECT --member=group:team-a@example.com --role=roles/compute.networkUser

questions.title: Who can turn a project into a Shared VPC host
questions.summary: Shared VPC requires an organisation and the Shared VPC Admin role, granted at the organisation or a folder.
questions.question: A network engineer who is Owner of project net-host cannot run gcloud compute shared-vpc enable net-host; the command fails on permissions. The project is in an organisation. What does the engineer need?

options.A: roles/owner on every future service project.
options.B: Shared VPC Admin, granted on the organisation or the folder.
options.C: roles/compute.networkUser on net-host.
options.D: roles/resourcemanager.projectCreator at the organisation.

explanation.summary: Enabling a host project and attaching service projects needs Shared VPC Admin at the organisation or folder level; project ownership alone is not enough.

option_breakdown.A: Ownership of service projects does not grant the Shared VPC administration permissions.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. Enabling a host project and attaching service projects needs Shared VPC Admin at the organisation or folder level; project ownership alone is not enough.
option_breakdown.C: Network User lets people use subnets, not configure Shared VPC.
option_breakdown.D: Project Creator creates projects; it confers no network administration.

questions.title: On-premises routes visible in only one region
questions.summary: With regional dynamic routing, Cloud Router's learned routes reach only its region; set global routing mode.
questions.question: An HA VPN and Cloud Router in europe-west4 learn the on-premises prefixes over BGP. VMs in europe-west4 reach on-premises, but VMs in us-central1 on the same VPC do not. What should you change?

options.A: Set the VPC network's dynamic routing mode to global.
options.B: Create a second HA VPN and Cloud Router in us-central1 only.
options.C: Add static routes for the on-premises prefixes in us-central1.
options.D: Peer the VPC with itself across regions.

explanation.summary: In regional mode a Cloud Router programs learned routes only in its own region; global dynamic routing makes them available to every region of the VPC.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. In regional mode a Cloud Router programs learned routes only in its own region; global dynamic routing makes them available to every region of the VPC.
option_breakdown.B: A second gateway would work but adds cost and management when a setting solves it.
option_breakdown.C: Static routes duplicate what BGP already provides and must be maintained by hand.
option_breakdown.D: A VPC cannot peer with itself.

questions.title: Encrypting traffic on a Dedicated Interconnect
questions.summary: Interconnect traffic is not encrypted by default; use MACsec or HA VPN over Cloud Interconnect.
questions.question: A bank carries 40 Gbps between its data centre and Google Cloud over Dedicated Interconnect. Its auditor now requires the traffic to be encrypted in transit on that private link. What should it use?

options.A: Nothing — Dedicated Interconnect traffic is always encrypted.
options.B: Replace the Interconnect with a single HA VPN over the internet.
options.C: MACsec for Cloud Interconnect on the links.
options.D: Private Google Access for on-premises hosts.

explanation.summary: Interconnect is private but not encrypted by default; MACsec encrypts traffic between the on-premises router and Google's edge (HA VPN over Cloud Interconnect is the IPsec alternative).

option_breakdown.A: The link is private, not encrypted.
option_breakdown.B: HA VPN over the internet cannot carry 40 Gbps on a single tunnel pair.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. Interconnect is private but not encrypted by default; MACsec encrypts traffic between the on-premises router and Google's edge (HA VPN over Cloud Interconnect is the IPsec alternative).
option_breakdown.D: Private Google Access is about reaching Google APIs; it encrypts nothing.

explanation.gcloud_command: # Cloud Interconnect > (connection) > Enable MACsec, then configure the pre-shared keys on the router

questions.title: A private link to AWS without the internet
questions.summary: Cross-Cloud Interconnect provides dedicated physical links between Google Cloud and another cloud.
questions.question: A company moves 30 Gbps of steady traffic between its Google Cloud VPC and its AWS VPCs. It wants dedicated bandwidth over physical links rather than VPN tunnels over the internet, and does not want to rent space in a colocation facility to build them. What should it use?

options.A: Cross-Cloud Interconnect to AWS.
options.B: HA VPN tunnels to AWS virtual private gateways.
options.C: VPC Network Peering with the AWS VPCs.
options.D: Direct Peering with Google's edge.

explanation.summary: Cross-Cloud Interconnect is a dedicated physical connection between Google's network and another cloud provider, set up by Google, at 10 or 100 Gbps.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. Cross-Cloud Interconnect is a dedicated physical connection between Google's network and another cloud provider, set up by Google, at 10 or 100 Gbps.
option_breakdown.B: HA VPN runs IPsec over the internet, which the company wants to avoid for this volume.
option_breakdown.C: VPC Network Peering connects Google Cloud VPCs only.
option_breakdown.D: Direct Peering reaches Google's public services, not a VPC, and not AWS.

explanation.gcloud_command: # Console > Network Connectivity > Cross-Cloud Interconnect > Create (choose AWS and a location pair)

questions.title: A custom domain and WAF for Cloud Run
questions.summary: Put Cloud Run behind a global external Application Load Balancer with a serverless NEG.
questions.question: A public Cloud Run service must be reachable at shop.example.com with a Google-managed certificate, and Cloud Armor must filter requests before they reach it. What should you deploy?

options.A: A global external Application Load Balancer with a serverless NEG.
options.B: An external passthrough Network Load Balancer with the Cloud Run URL as its backend.
options.C: A DNS CNAME from shop.example.com to the run.app URL, with Cloud Armor on the service.
options.D: An internal Application Load Balancer with a serverless NEG.

explanation.summary: A serverless NEG puts Cloud Run behind the external Application Load Balancer, which provides the managed certificate and the backend service Cloud Armor attaches to.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. A serverless NEG puts Cloud Run behind the external Application Load Balancer, which provides the managed certificate and the backend service Cloud Armor attaches to.
option_breakdown.B: Passthrough load balancers do not take serverless backends or terminate HTTPS.
option_breakdown.C: Cloud Armor attaches to load balancer backend services, not to a Cloud Run service directly.
option_breakdown.D: An internal load balancer is not reachable from the internet.

questions.title: Internal UDP service that must see client addresses
questions.summary: An internal passthrough Network Load Balancer carries TCP and UDP privately and preserves the client IP.
questions.question: A syslog collection service on a managed instance group receives UDP 514 from thousands of internal VMs. The collectors must see each sender's real IP address, and nothing may be exposed to the internet. Which load balancer should you use?

options.A: An internal Application Load Balancer.
options.B: An internal proxy Network Load Balancer.
options.C: An external passthrough Network Load Balancer with firewall rules limiting sources.
options.D: An internal passthrough Network Load Balancer.

explanation.summary: The internal passthrough Network Load Balancer handles UDP on a private address and forwards packets unproxied, so backends see the original client IP.

option_breakdown.A: Application Load Balancers handle HTTP(S), not UDP syslog.
option_breakdown.B: Proxy load balancers terminate connections, hiding the client address, and handle TCP only.
option_breakdown.C: An external load balancer exposes the service to the internet, which the requirement forbids.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. The internal passthrough Network Load Balancer handles UDP on a private address and forwards packets unproxied, so backends see the original client IP.

questions.title: A managed certificate stuck in provisioning
questions.summary: A Google-managed certificate provisions only after the domain's DNS points at the load balancer.
questions.question: A global external Application Load Balancer uses a Google-managed certificate for app.example.com, but the certificate has shown PROVISIONING for hours. The domain's A record still points at the old hosting provider. What should you do?

options.A: Point the A record at the load balancer's IP address, then wait.
options.B: Upload a self-signed certificate to replace it.
options.C: Delete and recreate the certificate every hour until it activates.
options.D: Switch the load balancer to Standard Tier.

explanation.summary: Google-managed certificates (with load balancer authorisation) are issued only once the domain resolves to the load balancer's IP; until then they stay in provisioning.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. Google-managed certificates (with load balancer authorisation) are issued only once the domain resolves to the load balancer's IP; until then they stay in provisioning.
option_breakdown.B: A self-signed certificate triggers browser warnings and does not fix the cause.
option_breakdown.C: Recreating it restarts the same check against the same wrong DNS record.
option_breakdown.D: Global load balancers require Premium Tier, and the tier has nothing to do with certificates.

questions.title: A console change that keeps reverting itself
questions.summary: Config Connector reconciles continuously, so a manual change to a managed resource is reverted.
questions.question: An engineer changes a Cloud Storage bucket's lifecycle rules in the console. Within minutes the old rules are back. The bucket is defined as a StorageBucket resource in a GKE cluster's GitOps repository. Why?

options.A: Cloud Storage restores the previous lifecycle configuration automatically after any edit.
options.B: An organisation policy blocks lifecycle changes made in the console.
options.C: Terraform state refreshes itself every few minutes and re-applies the rules.
options.D: Config Connector reconciled the bucket back to its definition in Git.

explanation.summary: Config Connector manages Google Cloud resources as Kubernetes objects and keeps reconciling them, so the definition in Git wins; the change must be made there.

option_breakdown.A: Cloud Storage has no such behaviour.
option_breakdown.B: An organisation policy would have refused the change, not reverted it later.
option_breakdown.C: Terraform reconciles only when someone runs it.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. Config Connector manages Google Cloud resources as Kubernetes objects and keeps reconciling them, so the definition in Git wins; the change must be made there.

explanation.gcloud_command: kubectl get storagebucket kestrel-media -n team-a -o yaml   # the source of truth

questions.title: What an AI terminal agent is allowed to change
questions.summary: An AI CLI agent acts with the credentials of the session it runs in; least privilege still applies.
questions.question: A developer runs an AI agent in the terminal, such as Gemini CLI, that can execute gcloud commands with approval. The developer is logged in to gcloud as a user with Owner on production. What is the sound way to limit what the agent can change?

options.A: Trust the agent's built-in judgement, since it is supplied by Google.
options.B: Disable Cloud Audit Logs so the agent's actions do not clutter them.
options.C: Run it as an identity with only the roles the task needs.
options.D: Give the agent a service-account key with Owner so its actions are separate from the developer's.

explanation.summary: The agent uses the credentials of the session it runs in, so its reach is exactly that identity's IAM roles; narrowing the identity is what limits it.

option_breakdown.A: The agent can do whatever its credentials allow; approval prompts are not a permission boundary.
option_breakdown.B: Audit logs are the record of what changed — the last thing to turn off.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. The agent uses the credentials of the session it runs in, so its reach is exactly that identity's IAM roles; narrowing the identity is what limits it.
option_breakdown.D: An Owner key is both a long-lived secret and the same excessive privilege.

questions.title: Undoing a bad Helm upgrade
questions.summary: helm rollback returns a release to an earlier revision recorded in its history.
questions.question: A helm upgrade of release web in namespace shop deployed a broken configuration. The previous release revision worked. What is the quickest correct way to return to it?

options.A: Delete the namespace and reinstall the chart from scratch.
options.B: Run helm history web -n shop, then helm rollback web REVISION -n shop.
options.C: Run terraform destroy on the cluster and recreate it.
options.D: Edit the Deployment's YAML by hand to match what it looked like before.

explanation.summary: Helm keeps a history of each release's revisions, and rollback redeploys a chosen earlier revision in one step.

option_breakdown.A: Deleting the namespace causes an outage and deletes everything else in it.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. Helm keeps a history of each release's revisions, and rollback redeploys a chosen earlier revision in one step.
option_breakdown.C: Destroying the cluster is out of all proportion to a bad release.
option_breakdown.D: Hand edits drift from Helm's record and are overwritten by the next upgrade.

explanation.gcloud_command:
helm history web -n shop
helm rollback web 3 -n shop

questions.title: A hand-made bucket brought under Terraform
questions.summary: Existing resources are adopted into Terraform with import, not deleted and recreated.
questions.question: A production bucket holding 30 TB was created by hand last year. The team now manages everything with Terraform and has written a matching google_storage_bucket resource. terraform plan wants to create the bucket, which would fail on the existing name. What should they do?

options.A: Delete the bucket and let Terraform recreate it.
options.B: Rename the resource in code so Terraform creates a second bucket.
options.C: Import the existing bucket into Terraform state, then plan again.
options.D: Remove the resource from code and manage the bucket in the console forever.

explanation.summary: Import records the real resource in Terraform's state against the resource block, after which plan shows only genuine differences.

option_breakdown.A: Deleting 30 TB of production data to satisfy a tool is never the answer.
option_breakdown.B: A second bucket does not bring the first under management.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. Import records the real resource in Terraform's state against the resource block, after which plan shows only genuine differences.
option_breakdown.D: Leaving it unmanaged is the drift the team is trying to end.

explanation.gcloud_command:
terraform import google_storage_bucket.media kestrel-prod-media
terraform plan

questions.title: Terraform without running it yourself
questions.summary: Infrastructure Manager runs Terraform as a managed service, storing state and history.
questions.question: A small platform team wants to keep writing Terraform but no longer wants to operate a CI runner, a state bucket and locking for it. Deployments should run as a service account with a recorded history of each apply. What should they use?

options.A: Deployment Manager.
options.B: Infrastructure Manager.
options.C: Config Connector on a new GKE cluster.
options.D: Cloud Shell, running terraform apply by hand.

explanation.summary: Infrastructure Manager is Google's managed Terraform service: it runs previews and applies as a service account and keeps state and revision history for you.

option_breakdown.A: Deployment Manager is deprecated and does not run Terraform.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. Infrastructure Manager is Google's managed Terraform service: it runs previews and applies as a service account and keeps state and revision history for you.
option_breakdown.C: Config Connector means rewriting as Kubernetes resources and operating a cluster.
option_breakdown.D: Manual applies from Cloud Shell have no pipeline, no service account and no history.

questions.title: AlloyDB that must outlive its region
questions.summary: AlloyDB's HA spans zones; for a regional outage add a secondary cluster in another region and promote it.
questions.question: An order service runs on an AlloyDB for PostgreSQL cluster in us-central1 with a highly available primary instance. The business now requires the database to be recoverable if the whole of us-central1 becomes unavailable. What should you configure?

options.A: A read pool instance with three nodes in the primary cluster.
options.B: A secondary cluster in another region, promoted if us-central1 fails.
options.C: Nothing more; the highly available primary instance already spans two regions.
options.D: A second primary instance in a different zone of us-central1.

explanation.summary: Cross-region replication in AlloyDB uses a secondary cluster in a different region. It receives the primary cluster's changes asynchronously and can be promoted to a standalone primary during a regional outage.

option_breakdown.A: Read pool nodes scale reads inside the same cluster and region; they do not protect against losing the region.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. Cross-region replication in AlloyDB uses a secondary cluster in a different region. It receives the primary cluster's changes asynchronously and can be promoted to a standalone primary during a regional outage.
option_breakdown.C: AlloyDB high availability places a standby in another zone of the same region, not another region.
option_breakdown.D: A cluster has one primary instance, and any zone of us-central1 fails together with the region.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud alloydb clusters create-secondary orders-dr --region=us-east4 \
  --primary-cluster=projects/P/locations/us-central1/clusters/orders
gcloud alloydb clusters promote orders-dr --region=us-east4   # during a regional outage

questions.title: A BigQuery dataset copy kept in a second region
questions.summary: Cross-region dataset replication keeps a read-only replica in a second region that can be promoted to primary.
questions.question: An analytics team keeps its curated BigQuery dataset in europe-west3. Auditors require a continuously updated copy of the dataset in europe-west4 that can take over as the writable copy if europe-west3 is lost. Which BigQuery feature meets this?

options.A: Table snapshots taken every hour.
options.B: Time travel with a seven-day window.
options.C: Cross-region dataset replication, with the replica promoted if needed.
options.D: A second dataset in the same location, refreshed by a scheduled query.

explanation.summary: Dataset replication keeps a secondary replica in another region in sync with the primary. The secondary is read-only until you switch it to be the primary.

option_breakdown.A: Snapshots are stored in the same location as the base table, so they are lost with the region.
option_breakdown.B: Time travel recovers earlier versions of data in the same location; it adds no second region.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. Dataset replication keeps a secondary replica in another region in sync with the primary. The secondary is read-only until you switch it to be the primary.
option_breakdown.D: A scheduled query copies data inside the same location and must be run and maintained by you.

explanation.gcloud_command:
ALTER SCHEMA curated ADD REPLICA `europe-west4` OPTIONS(location='europe-west4');
ALTER SCHEMA curated SET OPTIONS(primary_replica='europe-west4');   -- promote

questions.title: BigQuery failover that brings compute with the data
questions.summary: Managed disaster recovery (Enterprise Plus) fails over both slots and dataset replicas to the secondary region.
questions.question: A bank already replicates its BigQuery datasets to a second region. In a drill, the data was there after the primary region was lost, but the reporting jobs had no slot capacity to run in the secondary region. The bank wants storage and compute to fail over together. What does it need?

options.A: More on-demand quota in the secondary region.
options.B: A second dataset replica in a third region.
options.C: Managed disaster recovery, with an Enterprise Plus failover reservation.
options.D: Cross-region table copies scheduled every 15 minutes.

explanation.summary: Managed disaster recovery is an Enterprise Plus edition feature. A failover reservation has a secondary location, and datasets attached to it fail over with the slots, so compute is available in the promoted region.

option_breakdown.A: Quota is not reserved capacity, and it does not coordinate failover of the replicas.
option_breakdown.B: Another replica adds another copy of the data, but still no compute that fails over with it.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. Managed disaster recovery is an Enterprise Plus edition feature. A failover reservation has a secondary location, and datasets attached to it fail over with the slots, so compute is available in the promoted region.
option_breakdown.D: Copies move data, not slot capacity, and add their own lag and management work.

questions.title: No connection-string change after a Cloud SQL regional failover
questions.summary: Enterprise Plus advanced DR: a designated DR replica plus the write endpoint DNS name that follows the primary.
questions.question: A Cloud SQL for MySQL Enterprise Plus instance in europe-west1 has a cross-region replica in europe-west4. After the last DR drill, every application had to be reconfigured with the new primary's IP address. What should you set up so that applications keep working unchanged after a failover or switchover?

options.A: A designated DR replica, with applications using the write endpoint.
options.B: Reserve a static internal IP address and move it to the promoted replica.
options.C: Enable high availability on the primary instance.
options.D: Connect with the Cloud SQL Auth Proxy using the original instance connection name.

explanation.summary: In advanced disaster recovery, the write endpoint is a global DNS name that always resolves to the current primary instance. After a replica failover or switchover it points at the new primary without any client change.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. In advanced disaster recovery, the write endpoint is a global DNS name that always resolves to the current primary instance. After a replica failover or switchover it points at the new primary without any client change.
option_breakdown.B: Cloud SQL instance IP addresses cannot be moved between instances.
option_breakdown.C: High availability fails over between zones in europe-west1; it does not help when the region fails.
option_breakdown.D: The connection name identifies one instance; after failover the primary is a different instance.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud sql instances patch orders --failover-dr-replica-name=PROJECT:orders-dr
# applications connect to the write endpoint DNS name shown on the instance, not to an IP address

questions.title: A planned Cloud SQL region move with zero data loss
questions.summary: Switchover makes the primary read-only until lag is zero, then promotes the DR replica: no data loss.
questions.question: Your Cloud SQL Enterprise Plus primary in us-east1 has a designated DR replica in us-west1. For planned maintenance on the us-east1 side, you want the us-west1 instance to become primary with no data lost, and the old primary to keep replicating as the new DR replica. Which operation should you use?

options.A: A replica failover to the DR replica.
options.B: A switchover to the DR replica.
options.C: Promoting the replica with gcloud sql instances promote-replica, then recreating replication by hand.
options.D: An export of the primary to Cloud Storage and an import into the replica.

explanation.summary: Switchover is the planned operation: the primary stops accepting writes and becomes read-only, and the DR replica is promoted only once replication lag reaches zero. The roles reverse, so nothing is lost.

option_breakdown.A: Replica failover is for an outage; it promotes immediately and can lose data if the replica is lagging.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. Switchover is the planned operation: the primary stops accepting writes and becomes read-only, and the DR replica is promoted only once replication lag reaches zero. The roles reverse, so nothing is lost.
option_breakdown.C: A plain promotion breaks replication and leaves the topology to rebuild manually.
option_breakdown.D: An export and import is slow, needs downtime, and loses writes made after the export.

questions.title: Five nines inside one country for a relational database
questions.summary: A Spanner dual-region configuration keeps data in one country with the multi-region availability SLA.
questions.question: A German insurer needs a relational database with a 99.999% availability SLA that keeps running if one region fails. Regulation requires all replicas to stay inside Germany. Which Spanner instance configuration should it choose?

options.A: The regional configuration europe-west3.
options.B: The dual-region configuration dual-region-germany1.
options.C: The multi-region configuration eur3.
options.D: Two regional instances in europe-west3 and europe-west10 kept in sync by Dataflow.

explanation.summary: Dual-region configurations replicate across two regions in one country and carry the same 99.999% SLA as multi-region configurations, so they meet both the residency and the availability requirement.

option_breakdown.A: A regional configuration has a 99.99% SLA and does not survive the loss of its region.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. Dual-region configurations replicate across two regions in one country and carry the same 99.999% SLA as multi-region configurations, so they meet both the residency and the availability requirement.
option_breakdown.C: eur3 places replicas in Belgium and the Netherlands, outside Germany.
option_breakdown.D: Two instances synchronised by a pipeline are neither consistent nor covered by a 99.999% SLA.

questions.title: Putting a Spanner leader next to the writers
questions.summary: Move the default leader region to where most writes come from; it is cheap and moves no data.
questions.question: A Spanner database uses the multi-region configuration nam6. Almost all writes now come from services in us-east1, but write latency is high because the leader replicas are in another region. What is the least disruptive fix?

options.A: Create a new instance whose configuration includes us-east1 and migrate the data.
options.B: Add a read-only replica in us-east1.
options.C: Switch the application's writes to stale reads.
options.D: Change the database's default leader to us-east1.

explanation.summary: In dual-region and multi-region configurations you choose which read-write region holds the leaders. Changing the default leader takes a few minutes and involves no data movement.

option_breakdown.A: us-east1 is already a read-write region of nam6, so no migration is needed.
option_breakdown.B: Read-only replicas serve reads; they cannot hold leaders or accept writes.
option_breakdown.C: Stale reads relax read consistency; writes still go to the leader.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. In dual-region and multi-region configurations you choose which read-write region holds the leaders. Changing the default leader takes a few minutes and involves no data movement.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud spanner databases ddl update orders --instance=prod \
  --ddl="ALTER DATABASE orders SET OPTIONS (default_leader = 'us-east1')"

questions.title: Stale reads after adding a Bigtable cluster in another region
questions.summary: Replication is eventually consistent; a job that must read its own writes uses single-cluster routing.
questions.question: A Bigtable instance was given a second cluster in another region, and applications moved to an app profile with multi-cluster routing. Since then, a job that writes a row and immediately reads it back sometimes gets the old value. What should you change for that job?

options.A: Turn replication off while the job runs.
options.B: Add a third cluster so replication finishes sooner.
options.C: An app profile with single-cluster routing for that job.
options.D: Move the job to an app profile that uses multi-cluster routing to the nearest cluster.

explanation.summary: Replication between Bigtable clusters is eventually consistent. With multi-cluster routing, a read can reach a cluster that has not yet received the write. Single-cluster routing gives that workload read-your-writes consistency.

option_breakdown.A: Removing replication gives up the second region's redundancy for every workload.
option_breakdown.B: More clusters add replication paths; they do not make replication synchronous.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. Replication between Bigtable clusters is eventually consistent. With multi-cluster routing, a read can reach a cluster that has not yet received the write. Single-cluster routing gives that workload read-your-writes consistency.
option_breakdown.D: That is the current setup, which is what allows reads to reach a different cluster.

questions.title: A VM data disk replicated to another region every minute
questions.summary: Asynchronous Replication copies a disk to a secondary region with a target RPO of about one minute.
questions.question: A self-managed database runs on a Compute Engine VM with a zonal Persistent Disk in europe-west1. The disaster-recovery plan requires a copy of the disk in europe-west4 that is at most about a minute behind. What should you use?

options.A: A regional Persistent Disk replicated across two zones of europe-west1.
options.B: Persistent Disk Asynchronous Replication to a disk in europe-west4.
options.C: A snapshot schedule that runs every hour and stores snapshots in europe-west4.
options.D: A machine image of the VM created every night.

explanation.summary: Asynchronous Replication copies a disk to a secondary disk in another region with a target RPO of about one minute. If the primary region fails, you fail over and attach the secondary disk to a VM there.

option_breakdown.A: A regional disk copies synchronously within one region, so it is lost with that region.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. Asynchronous Replication copies a disk to a secondary disk in another region with a target RPO of about one minute. If the primary region fails, you fail over and attach the secondary disk to a VM there.
option_breakdown.C: Snapshot schedules cannot run more often than hourly, far above a one-minute RPO.
option_breakdown.D: A nightly machine image has an RPO of up to a day.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud compute disks create db-data-dr --zone=europe-west4-a \
  --primary-disk=db-data --primary-disk-zone=europe-west1-b
gcloud compute disks start-async-replication db-data --zone=europe-west1-b \
  --secondary-disk=db-data-dr --secondary-disk-zone=europe-west4-a

questions.title: The RPO of a multi-region bucket you have not tuned
questions.summary: Default replication: 99.9% of new objects within an hour, all within 12 hours. Turbo exists only for dual-regions.
questions.question: A media company stores masters in a bucket in the EU multi-region with default settings. The DR runbook must state the recovery point objective for objects in that bucket. What should it say?

options.A: Every object is written synchronously to two regions, so the RPO is zero.
options.B: Fifteen minutes, because turbo replication applies to all multi-region buckets.
options.C: About an hour for most new objects, and up to 12 hours for all.
options.D: There is no second copy until you configure Object Versioning.

explanation.summary: Default replication targets 99.9% of newly written objects within one hour and 100% within 12 hours. Turbo replication, with a 15-minute RPO, applies only to dual-region buckets.

option_breakdown.A: Replication between regions is asynchronous, so the RPO is not zero.
option_breakdown.B: Turbo replication cannot be enabled on multi-region buckets.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. Default replication targets 99.9% of newly written objects within one hour and 100% within 12 hours. Turbo replication, with a 15-minute RPO, applies only to dual-region buckets.
option_breakdown.D: Versioning keeps older generations of an object; it is unrelated to geo-redundancy.

questions.title: NetApp volumes that survive a regional outage
questions.summary: Google Cloud NetApp Volumes volume replication keeps a destination volume in another region.
questions.question: A design studio serves project files from a Google Cloud NetApp Volumes SMB volume in us-west1. It needs a copy of the volume in us-east4 that can be made writable if us-west1 is unavailable. What should it configure?

options.A: Volume snapshots on an hourly schedule.
options.B: Volume replication to a destination volume in us-east4.
options.C: A Filestore Regional instance in us-west1.
options.D: A backup to a backup vault in us-west1.

explanation.summary: NetApp Volumes volume replication asynchronously copies a volume to a destination volume in another region. The destination is read-only until you stop replication, which makes it writable.

option_breakdown.A: Snapshots live with the volume and are lost if its region is unavailable.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. NetApp Volumes volume replication asynchronously copies a volume to a destination volume in another region. The destination is read-only until you stop replication, which makes it writable.
option_breakdown.C: Filestore Regional protects against zone failures within one region and is a different product.
option_breakdown.D: A backup vault in the same region fails together with the source.

explanation.gcloud_command:
# Console > NetApp Volumes > Volumes > projects-share > Replication > Create replication
#   destination: a storage pool in us-east4; stop replication to make the destination writable

questions.title: Cloud SQL backups stored outside the instance's region
questions.summary: Set a custom backup location (another region or a multi-region) so backups survive the regional outage.
questions.question: A Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL instance runs in asia-south1, and its backups are configured to be stored in asia-south1. Compliance requires that, if asia-south1 is unavailable, the latest automated backups can still be restored elsewhere. The team does not want a running replica. What should it change?

options.A: Increase backup retention to 365 backups.
options.B: A custom backup location in another region, such as asia-south2.
options.C: Enable point-in-time recovery.
options.D: Enable deletion protection on the instance.

explanation.summary: Backups stored in the instance's own region are lost with it. A custom backup location puts them in a region or multi-region you choose, so they stay available when the instance's region is not.

option_breakdown.A: Keeping more backups does not change where they are stored.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. Backups stored in the instance's own region are lost with it. A custom backup location puts them in a region or multi-region you choose, so they stay available when the instance's region is not.
option_breakdown.C: Point-in-time recovery uses the same backups and logs; it does not add a location.
option_breakdown.D: Deletion protection prevents accidental deletion; it does not affect regional failure.

questions.title: An existing MongoDB application moving to a serverless database
questions.summary: Firestore with MongoDB compatibility runs MongoDB drivers and queries on serverless Firestore.
questions.question: A startup runs a document-based application written against the MongoDB drivers and query language. It wants a fully managed, serverless Google Cloud database with multi-region replication and no capacity planning, while changing as little application code as possible. What should it choose?

options.A: Bigtable with a column family per collection.
options.B: Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL with JSONB columns.
options.C: MongoDB installed on a managed instance group of Compute Engine VMs.
options.D: Firestore with MongoDB compatibility.

explanation.summary: Firestore with MongoDB compatibility, part of Firestore Enterprise edition, accepts standard MongoDB drivers and MQL on Firestore's serverless infrastructure. It offers multi-region replication with a 99.999% SLA.

option_breakdown.A: Bigtable needs a rewrite to its wide-column API and does not speak MongoDB.
option_breakdown.B: PostgreSQL JSONB requires rewriting every query in SQL.
option_breakdown.C: Running MongoDB yourself is the operational work the team wants to avoid.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. Firestore with MongoDB compatibility, part of Firestore Enterprise edition, accepts standard MongoDB drivers and MQL on Firestore's serverless infrastructure. It offers multi-region replication with a 99.999% SLA.

questions.title: NFS that keeps serving when a zone fails
questions.summary: Filestore Regional replicates the file share across zones in one region for a 99.99% SLA.
questions.question: A content management system on a regional managed instance group mounts an NFS share. A recent zonal outage took the share down even though the VMs in the other zones stayed up. What should the share run on?

options.A: A Filestore Basic HDD instance.
options.B: A Filestore Zonal instance with a larger capacity.
options.C: A Filestore Regional instance.
options.D: A Cloud Storage bucket mounted through Cloud Storage FUSE, used as the NFS share.

explanation.summary: Filestore Regional stores data redundantly across zones in the region, so the share stays available when a zone fails, matching the instance group's own zonal redundancy.

option_breakdown.A: Basic instances live in a single zone.
option_breakdown.B: More capacity does not add zonal redundancy to a zonal instance.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. Filestore Regional stores data redundantly across zones in the region, so the share stays available when a zone fails, matching the instance group's own zonal redundancy.
option_breakdown.D: FUSE is not NFS and lacks full POSIX semantics such as file locking.

questions.title: A BigQuery multi-region is not a second region
questions.summary: No: a BigQuery multi-region stores data in one region within the geography; use replication or managed DR.
questions.question: A team created its BigQuery datasets in the US multi-region and assumes this protects them against the loss of an entire Google Cloud region. What is true?

options.A: The assumption holds; US multi-region datasets are stored synchronously in at least two regions.
options.B: They are protected only if Object Versioning is enabled on the datasets.
options.C: They are protected once time travel is extended to seven days.
options.D: It isn't protected: a multi-region dataset has no second-region copy by default.

explanation.summary: Choosing a BigQuery multi-region stores the data in a single region within that geography, redundant across zones only. BigQuery does not keep a copy in another region unless you configure one.

option_breakdown.A: That is how Cloud Storage multi-region buckets behave, not BigQuery datasets.
option_breakdown.B: Object Versioning is a Cloud Storage feature, not a BigQuery one.
option_breakdown.C: Time travel keeps history in the same location.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. Choosing a BigQuery multi-region stores the data in a single region within that geography, redundant across zones only. BigQuery does not keep a copy in another region unless you configure one.

explanation.gcloud_command: ALTER SCHEMA analytics ADD REPLICA `us-west1` OPTIONS(location='us-west1');

questions.title: Daily Filestore protection that survives the region
questions.summary: Filestore backups can be created in another region and restored to any region.
questions.question: A Filestore Zonal instance in us-central1 holds build caches that can tolerate a day of data loss. The team wants the cheapest way to be able to rebuild the share in us-east1 if us-central1 is unavailable. What should it do?

options.A: Take daily Filestore snapshots of the instance.
options.B: A daily Filestore backup stored in us-east1, restored there if needed.
options.C: Change the instance to the Regional tier.
options.D: Copy the share to a second VM's local SSD every night.

explanation.summary: Filestore backups are independent of the source instance, can be stored in a different region, and can be restored to an instance in any region.

option_breakdown.A: Snapshots are stored on the instance itself and disappear with its region.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. Filestore backups are independent of the source instance, can be stored in a different region, and can be restored to an instance in any region.
option_breakdown.C: The Regional tier protects against zone failures, not the loss of us-central1.
option_breakdown.D: Local SSD data is ephemeral and the VM would still be in a region you choose by hand.

questions.title: A Bigtable backup kept outside the source region
questions.summary: Copy a Bigtable backup to a cluster in another region with gcloud bigtable backups copy.
questions.question: A single-cluster Bigtable instance in europe-west1 is backed up nightly. The team does not want to pay for a second replicated cluster, but it must be able to restore last night's data if europe-west1 is lost. What should it add to the nightly job?

options.A: Increase the backup's expiration time to 90 days.
options.B: Export the table to a Cloud Storage bucket in europe-west1.
options.C: Add an app profile with multi-cluster routing.
options.D: Copy each new backup to a cluster in another region.

explanation.summary: A Bigtable backup is stored with its cluster. Copying it to a cluster in another region gives a restorable copy that survives the source region.

option_breakdown.A: Keeping the backup longer does not change where it is stored.
option_breakdown.B: An export kept in europe-west1 is lost along with the region.
option_breakdown.C: Multi-cluster routing needs a second cluster, which the team does not want, and is not a backup.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. A Bigtable backup is stored with its cluster. Copying it to a cluster in another region gives a restorable copy that survives the source region.

questions.title: Standing instructions for Gemini CLI in a repository
questions.summary: A GEMINI.md context file in the project gives Gemini CLI persistent conventions and instructions.
questions.question: Every time engineers use Gemini CLI in the infrastructure repository, they repeat the same instructions: use Terraform modules from modules/, name resources with the team prefix, and never use default VPCs. How can they give Gemini CLI these instructions once?

options.A: Add them as comments at the top of main.tf.
options.B: A GEMINI.md context file at the repository root.
options.C: Save them as a gcloud configuration property.
options.D: Store them in Secret Manager and reference the secret in each prompt.

explanation.summary: Gemini CLI reads GEMINI.md context files in the project hierarchy and includes them in every session, so conventions are applied without being repeated.

option_breakdown.A: Comments in one file are seen only when that file is read, not as standing instructions.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. Gemini CLI reads GEMINI.md context files in the project hierarchy and includes them in every session, so conventions are applied without being repeated.
option_breakdown.C: gcloud properties configure the gcloud CLI, not Gemini CLI.
option_breakdown.D: Secrets hold sensitive values; this is ordinary guidance and would still need pasting.

explanation.gcloud_command:
cat > GEMINI.md <<'EOF'
- Use modules from ./modules
- Prefix resource names with plat-
- Never use the default VPC
EOF

questions.title: Giving Gemini CLI a new tool through MCP
questions.summary: Register an MCP server in Gemini CLI's settings.json so the agent can call its tools.
questions.question: The platform team runs a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that exposes read-only tools over its internal service catalogue. Engineers want Gemini CLI to call those tools during planning. What should they do?

options.A: Register the MCP server in Gemini CLI's settings file.
options.B: Deploy the MCP server as a Cloud Run function named gemini-cli.
options.C: Paste the catalogue into each prompt.
options.D: Add the server's URL to the repository's GEMINI.md file.

explanation.summary: Gemini CLI discovers tools from the MCP servers configured in its settings. Once registered, the agent can call the server's tools during a session.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. Gemini CLI discovers tools from the MCP servers listed under mcpServers in its settings.json; once registered, the agent can call them during a session.
option_breakdown.B: Where the server runs does not register it with Gemini CLI.
option_breakdown.C: Pasting data loses the tool interface and is repetitive and error-prone.
option_breakdown.D: GEMINI.md gives the agent instructions and context; it doesn't register tools.

questions.title: From a plain-language description to a deployable design
questions.summary: Gemini Cloud Assist in Application Design Center turns a description into an architecture you can refine and deploy.
questions.question: A product engineer describes a new service in a sentence: "a public web app on Cloud Run, backed by Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL, with images in Cloud Storage". They want a proposed architecture they can refine and then deploy, without writing Terraform first. What should they use?

options.A: Cloud Asset Inventory.
options.B: Active Assist recommendations.
options.C: Gemini Cloud Assist in Application Design Center.
options.D: Config Connector.

explanation.summary: Gemini Cloud Assist can generate an application design from a natural-language description in Application Design Center, showing the components and their connections for refinement and deployment.

option_breakdown.A: Asset Inventory reports what already exists; it does not design anything.
option_breakdown.B: Active Assist optimises existing resources.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. Gemini Cloud Assist can generate an application design from a natural-language description in Application Design Center, showing the components and their connections for refinement and deployment.
option_breakdown.D: Config Connector manages resources declared as Kubernetes objects; you still write them yourself.

explanation.gcloud_command: # Console > Application Design Center > Create application > describe it to Gemini Cloud Assist

questions.title: Gemini Cloud Assist from a third-party AI tool
questions.summary: Gemini Cloud Assist exposes a remote MCP server so external MCP clients can use its capabilities.
questions.question: An SRE team does its incident work in a third-party AI assistant that supports the Model Context Protocol. It wants that assistant to use Gemini Cloud Assist's knowledge of their Google Cloud projects. What should it configure?

options.A: A Pub/Sub topic that forwards console events to the assistant.
options.B: Gemini Cloud Assist's remote MCP server, added to the assistant.
options.C: A service account key for the assistant with roles/owner.
options.D: A BigQuery export of Cloud Asset Inventory shared with the assistant's vendor.

explanation.summary: Gemini Cloud Assist provides a remote MCP server. MCP-capable clients connect to it and call Gemini Cloud Assist with the signed-in user's permissions.

option_breakdown.A: Console events are not how Gemini Cloud Assist is integrated.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. Gemini Cloud Assist provides a remote MCP server. MCP-capable clients connect to it and call Gemini Cloud Assist with the signed-in user's permissions.
option_breakdown.C: Owner keys are a serious security risk and still do not provide Gemini Cloud Assist.
option_breakdown.D: Sharing inventory exports with a vendor exposes data and gives no assistant capability.

explanation.gcloud_command: # In the MCP client: add the Gemini Cloud Assist remote MCP server endpoint and sign in with Google

questions.title: Remote 3D design workstations
questions.summary: Graphics workloads need GPUs with virtual workstation (RTX vWS) support; TPUs do not render graphics.
questions.question: An architecture firm wants to move 30 designers' CAD and 3D rendering desktops to Google Cloud and stream them to thin clients. Which accelerator choice fits?

options.A: Cloud TPU v5e slices.
options.B: VMs with NVIDIA L4 GPUs and RTX Virtual Workstation images.
options.C: C3 VMs with no accelerator and more vCPUs.
options.D: A GKE cluster with TPU node pools.

explanation.summary: Interactive 3D graphics need GPUs with graphics drivers. Compute Engine offers NVIDIA RTX Virtual Workstation images for GPUs such as the L4.

option_breakdown.A: TPUs accelerate matrix operations for machine learning; they cannot drive graphics.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. Interactive 3D graphics need GPUs with graphics drivers. Compute Engine offers NVIDIA RTX Virtual Workstation images for GPUs such as the L4.
option_breakdown.C: CPU rendering is far too slow for interactive 3D work.
option_breakdown.D: TPU node pools are for ML training and serving, not graphics.

questions.title: Training across thousands of tightly linked accelerators
questions.summary: Very large TensorFlow/JAX training suits multi-host TPU slices with high-speed inter-chip interconnect.
questions.question: A research lab will pre-train a very large JAX model for weeks across thousands of accelerator chips. Its code has no custom CUDA kernels, and cost per training step is the main criterion. What should it plan to use?

options.A: Thousands of single-GPU N1 VMs in a managed instance group.
options.B: Spot C3 VMs with many vCPUs each.
options.C: Cloud Run jobs with GPUs attached.
options.D: A multi-host Cloud TPU slice.

explanation.summary: TPU slices are built for large-scale training. Frameworks such as JAX use the inter-chip interconnect to scale across hosts efficiently, typically with strong price-performance.

option_breakdown.A: Loosely connected single-GPU VMs scale poorly for synchronous training at this size.
option_breakdown.B: CPUs are far too slow for this workload.
option_breakdown.C: Cloud Run jobs are not built for weeks-long, tightly coupled training across thousands of chips.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. TPU slices are built for large-scale training. Frameworks such as JAX use the inter-chip interconnect to scale across hosts efficiently, typically with strong price-performance.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud compute tpus queued-resources create pretrain --node-id=pt --zone=us-east5-a \
  --accelerator-type=v5p-2048 --runtime-version=RUNTIME_VERSION

questions.title: Filestore that can be promoted in another region
questions.summary: Filestore instance replication keeps a standby instance in another region (RPO about 30 minutes).
